facts.text: The Connecticut General Assembly authorized the creation of a village in Wallingford Center on October 10, 1667, for thirty-eight planters and freemen.
Wallingford was officially incorporated in 1670, with about 126 people settling in the town in temporary housing that same year.
Wallingford Center is a historic district featuring a walkable downtown with boutique shops and estates ranging from Colonial to Victorian styles.
During the nineteenth century, Wallingford industry expanded with a significant concentration of small pewter and Britannia ware manufacturers.
Robert Wallace established the forerunner of Wallace Silversmiths in Wallingford after acquiring the formula for nickel silver by mid-century.
Several plants in Wallingford eventually combined with other small silver and Britannia plants to form the International Silver Company.
